findings.title: Migration crashes when no embed category is configured
findings.body: This query returns no rows when `embed_category` has not been explicitly stored or does not match a category, but the next expression immediately indexes `[0]['id']`. Most installations without a configured embedding category will therefore raise during migration and be unable to upgrade. Handle the empty result before selecting the uncategorized fallback.

findings.title: Configured hosts with ports are never recognized
findings.body: Host values may include a port according to the validation regex and are stored with that port, but `URI(host).host` strips the port before this comparison. An entry such as `example.com:8080` therefore cannot match a referer or embed URL, so that configured host is rejected and its category mapping is not applied.

findings.title: Migration cannot be rolled back without losing the old settings
findings.body: This `change` migration deletes the legacy host and category settings with raw SQL, and the other raw `execute` calls have no inverse. Rails cannot automatically reverse these operations, so rolling back raises `ActiveRecord::IrreversibleMigration`; even a manual rollback cannot restore the deleted configuration unless it was separately preserved. Provide an explicit reversible migration that restores the old settings.
